title: Drowning Girl
lede: Roy Lichtenstein’s romance-comic close-up: a crying woman in a stylized wave, with a thought balloon that reads “I DON’T CARE! I’D RATHER SINK — THAN CALL BRAD FOR HELP!”
summary: A square close-up with dot-tinted skin, flat blue hair, heavy black waves, and a thought balloon. Roy Lichtenstein, 1963.

source.label: Roy Lichtenstein: A Catalogue Raisonné, Drowning Girl (RLCR 761)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the catalogue raisonné image of the Museum of Modern Art’s painting, MoMA 685.1971 (1180 × 1200 px), in a scratchpad. MoMA’s own page blocks scripts. No image is stored.

styles.note: A canonical romance-comic panel: dot-tinted skin, even black key lines, flat primary blue, and a thought balloon with hand-lettered capitals.

context: The catalogue raisonné gives acrylic, oil, and graphite pencil on canvas, 171.8 × 169.5 cm, and the source as *Secret Hearts* #83 (November 1962). The Museum of Modern Art acquired it in December 1971 (685.1971). [RLCR 761](https://www.lichtensteincatalogue.org/catalogue/entry.php?id=452).

It was shown in Lichtenstein’s September–October 1963 exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery, the show announced by the [Crak! poster](ref:lichtenstein-crak-poster-1963). [RLCR 761](https://www.lichtensteincatalogue.org/catalogue/entry.php?id=452).
Wikipedia reports that the work also borrows from Hokusai’s *The Great Wave off Kanagawa*. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowning_Girl).
observed: The face, hand, and arm are filled with fine red dots on white; the lips are flat pink with a black outline.
The hair is solid ultramarine blue with black strands. No blue dots appear in the hair.
The water is a pattern of heavy black curls and white foam shapes on a pale blue dot field.
A white thought balloon with a scalloped outline and three small bubbles fills the upper left. It holds four lines of black hand-lettered capitals.
Tears are drawn as white drops with black outlines.
Black outlines vary from thick to very thick. There are no gradients or modeled shadows.
interpretation: The painting shows the romance branch of the idiom: close-up faces, a limited palette of dot-red skin and one solid primary, and text in a balloon, not a caption box.
Large black shapes carry as much of the design as the outlines do. The style is not only outline plus fill; solid black areas give it weight.
borrow: Use a scalloped thought balloon for a quote or testimonial, with small trailing bubbles.
Tint large areas with a pale dot field and reserve one strong solid color for the focal shape.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The catalogue raisonné states “© 2026 Roy Lichtenstein Foundation. All Rights Reserved.”
